[cols="2,2,2,6,3",options="header"]
|===
|Family |Target |Default |Why |Tested by

|AES-GCM
|native, Clang and GCC
|OpenSSL
|OpenSSL's assembly uses the CPU's AES and carry-less multiplication instructions on x86-64 and ARMv8 (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/aes/asm[OpenSSL's AES assembly for ARMv8 and x86-64]; link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/modes/asm[OpenSSL's GHASH and AES-GCM assembly]); BearSSL has them on x86 only (link:https://www.bearssl.org/support.html[BearSSL, the AES implementations it selects]). OpenSSL whatever the program links: a program that links BearSSL alone names `gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>`
|`+default_both+`, `+default_backend_all_linked+`

|AES-GCM
|native, MSVC
|OpenSSL
|the same rule as with Clang and GCC, but here OpenSSL is built no-asm: table-based AES and 4-bit GHASH, no AES-NI, not constant time (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md[OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm]); where timing attacks matter, link BearSSL and name `gcm<aes256<backends::bearssl>>`
|`+default_both+`

|AES-GCM
|wasip2, wasip3
|BearSSL
|constant time by design (link:https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html[BearSSL, constant-time crypto]), where OpenSSL is built no-asm and its AES and GHASH are table-based (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md[OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm]). BearSSL whatever the program links: a program that links OpenSSL alone names `gcm<aes256<backends::openssl>>`
|`+default_bearssl+`, `+default_both_wasm+`, `+default_backend_all_linked+`

|AES-GCM
|emscripten
|BearSSL
|the only AES-GCM backend there: webcpp does not build OpenSSL for Emscripten
|`+default_bearssl+`, `+default_backend_all_linked_emscripten+`

|AES block cipher
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|none
|a raw block cipher is a building block a program chooses deliberately, naming its backend; `aes256<>` takes AES-GCM's default as its argument, and its `make` does not compile where that is BearSSL
|`+default_backend_none_linked+`, `+default_selection_bearssl+`

|secp256k1
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsecp256k1
|the only backend (link:https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1#readme[libsecp256k1's README])
|`+secp256k1+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|Ed25519
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend in this version, on every target, and its verification is the policy `strict` (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/public-key_signatures[libsodium's documentation, public-key signatures]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032[RFC 8032, the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)])
|`+ed25519_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|X25519
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend in this version, on every target; it refuses an all-zero shared secret itself (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7748[RFC 7748, Elliptic Curves for Security (X25519 and X448)])
|`+x25519_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|crypto_kx
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own construction, whose session keys only another `crypto_kx` derives (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/key_exchange[libsodium's documentation, key exchange])
|`+kx_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|PEM
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend in this version, on every target; its base64 runs in a time that does not depend on the bytes, a private key's in a PKCS#8 (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/helpers#base64-encoding-decoding[libsodium's documentation, helpers: base64 encoding and decoding])
|`+formats_25519_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|ChaCha20-Poly1305
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|one library for the three ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEADs on every target, where BearSSL and OpenSSL have RFC 8439's alone (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305[libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions]); a program that links BearSSL or OpenSSL alone names it in the type, as in `chacha20_poly1305<backends::bearssl>`
|`+chacha_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|original ChaCha20-Poly1305
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305[libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions])
|`+chacha_original_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|XChaCha20-Poly1305
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305[libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions])
|`+xchacha_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|XSalsa20-Poly1305 secret box
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, NaCl's `crypto_secretbox`, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox[libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption])
|`+secretbox_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|XChaCha20-Poly1305 secret box
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox[libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption])
|`+secretbox_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 box
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, NaCl's `crypto_box`, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/authenticated_encryption[libsodium's documentation, public-key authenticated encryption])
|`+box_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|X25519-XChaCha20-Poly1305 box
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/authenticated_encryption[libsodium's documentation, public-key authenticated encryption])
|`+box_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|X25519-XSalsa20-Poly1305 sealed box
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsodium
|the only backend that has it: libsodium's own C code, which draws the key pair of each message from its own generator, the same on every target (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/public-key_cryptography/sealed_boxes[libsodium's documentation, sealed boxes])
|`+box_sodium+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|ElligatorSwift
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsecp256k1
|the only backend (link:https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1#readme[libsecp256k1's README])
|`+secp256k1_ellswift+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|MuSig2
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsecp256k1
|the only backend (link:https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1#readme[libsecp256k1's README])
|`+secp256k1_musig+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|BIP 352 silent payments
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|libsecp256k1
|the only backend (link:https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1#readme[libsecp256k1's README])
|`+secp256k1_silent_payments+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`

|P-256
|native, wasip2, wasip3, emscripten
|BearSSL
|the one backend of the P-curves on all four targets, constant time by design and allocating nothing (link:https://www.bearssl.org/[BearSSL, its home page]); OpenSSL and Botan join in increments 8 and 7
|`+p256_keys_bearssl+`, `+p256_ecdsa_bearssl+`, `+p256_ecdh_bearssl+`, `+default_backend_none_linked+`
|===
